This game really surprised me with how engaging it was to pretend to be a hacker. Although some of the best bits were in the DLC, the base game and the concept here worked really well and had a lot of fun elements. It can basically be boiled down to a puzzle game, figuring out how systems connect and how to break into them. It's an excellent touch that a lot of your actions are done through a command prompt. Once you're in the DLC section, puzzles get more involved and have a lot more steps and there are more complexities to solve. Having a IRC chat where characters interact was great, especially since the devs could sneakily insert helpful tips inside the context of the game. In total I played about 10 hours to complete the game with the DLC.

[spoiler] There's an excellent bit where you get hacked and you "crash", then it makes you use your actual command prompt on your desktop with a word file to help you delete a real file on your harddrive to allow you to launch the game again. That was very clever and a highlight of the game. The ending with the timed part where you have a make a quick moral decision was rough, since I knew what I wanted to do but wasn't fast enough to do it. [/spoiler]

You can refer back to the commands and what they do anytime.

It doesn't really require any technical knowledge, so as long as you're not deathly allergic to command-lines you can play it and have fun. The Labyrinths DLC is practically a second game in the same engine, too, in terms of its depth and complexity, and certainly worth it.

Story is ok- the main enjoyment comes out of the individual missions (enjoyment of each mission will vary depending on your preferences). The main story feels kinda short. I got the DLC 'Labyrinths' too which adds a good 2-3 hours extra content (and honestly I'd say some of the missions in that DLC are harder than the final missions of the maingame story)

As always, music is a big part of what makes a game great or not. In this case the choice of music is good, which really adds to the immersion. On a scale of 1-10 I'd rate the soundtrack at between 6 and 7. Its not the most amazing you'll ever hear but it benefits the game well and there are a couple of songs that are really good.

Some of the missions really make you think so expect to get stuck for a while at certain points- I certainly did. Just as a word of advice though- if something doesn't work, maybe you aren't doing it on the right machine! There should be no need to resort to a walkthrough as it ruins the experience (this is a puzzle solving game- if you aren't solving the puzzles yourself it defeats the point).

So to sum up- get this if you enjoy a casual/sometimes a bit tricky puzzle game with a terminal interface

This game is just like UPLink with better GUI.

[b]Cons[/b]
Gameplay is pretty repetative, terminal simulation is just awful:
[list]
    [*] The command are real, but they don't behave the real way. Why 'mv myFile myFolder/.' not only moves the file but also renames it??
    [*] Wildcard is used only when it is not surrounded with char, so no way to use 'rm myFile*' to delete both 'myFile1' and 'myFile2'. It just says 'No such file'
    [*] Tab-autocompletion worked better in Nokia 3310 than here. It works only in the top level, so no autocompleteion when you type 'cd folder/<TAB>' which made me actually traverse thru every folder, instead of going right where I needed to.
    [*] Why the hell 'scp' instead of 'cp'???
    [*] We're in UNIX world, and all our 'hacking' tools have 'exe' extension... Really???
[/list]

[b]Pros[/b]
The idea is interesting, there are a lot of pieces of different information scattered around the servers. I really like the idea of typing commands instead of clicking with the mouse. Nice idea with mimicing to 'man' :)

[b]Overall[/b]
Nice game, with a bit repetative gameplay. The game was killed by stupid terminal implementation.
But authors, really, RTFM... or at least support wildcards and dots properly in your terminal...

I found this game fun because you play a "wannabe hacker" who receives a mail from a famous hacker, your mentor.
Well it actually is a really simplified way on how things work but hey it's an indie game, not a AAA simulation.
I recommend it, it's a short game with a cool short story and relatively easy achievements to get.

The concept itself is very solid, but the game gets pretty damn repetitive halfway through. Still, a way better representation of actual hacking rather than some puzzle game Watch Dogs, or simply Hollywood two-people-on-one-keyboard bs.

Recommended if you like console-like interfaces and the concept of hacking. Although real life doesn't give you a simple porthack.exe tool.
